rfam.comment: The physiological role of Escherichia coli Spot 42 (spf) RNA has remained obscure, even though the 109-nucleotide RNA was discovered almost three decades ago. Spot 42 seems to have a regulatory role on the galactose operon [1]. It is proposed that Spot 42 acts by an antisense mechanism where the RNA binds to the galK translation initiator region [1]. Changes in Spot 42 levels are implicated in affecting the adjacent DNA polymerase I levels [2]. The Hfq protein has been shown to interact with several small regulatory RNAs in E. coli, and the protein is required for OxyS, DsrA, RprA and Spot 42 RNA regulation [3].
